title: Limits talk with access
openingNarrative: Someone starts a treatment-limits conversation. Address Rohan with AAC first. Silence or WAIT is not consent. Family may witness and support — they are not the decision workforce. Disability does not make escalation less worthwhile.
clinicalState: Accessible dialogue window. Cardiac instability may recur. No dose or energy trainers.

choices.label: Ask Rohan first; wait through slow AAC; document his framing
choices.immediateConsequence: Authorship and communication access rise; the conversation takes longer.
choices.delayedConsequence: Limits language stays about burdens and goals, not worth of life.

choices.label: Ask family to summarise goals before Rohan finishes answering
choices.immediateConsequence: Speed rises; authorship and trust fall.
choices.delayedConsequence: Silence was treated as something to fill — a dignity hit in debrief.

disabilityRightsNotes: Limits talk requires accessible communication — not family proxy first.
debriefNotes: Episode 02 tests accessible limits talk under cardiac instability.
